headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 14 of the 25 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in Northern Vermont and White Mountains. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
High pressure continues through Friday with increasing fire weather concerns on Thursday into Friday with slightly stronger winds and low humidity values.
Quiet weather continues into early next week with a cooling temperature trend.

ALY.excerpt: ) No significant weather through at least Monday with high confidence in dry weather persisting.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure remains in control of the weather pattern across northern New England through the weekend while an ocean storm passes offshore. Northerly gusts of 30 to 35 MPH possible later Thursday into Friday.

BUF.excerpt: ) Dry and tranquil weather will prevail through this weekend.

PHI.excerpt:
A nor'easter well off the coast will bring coastal impacts and hazardous marine conditions through Thursday.
A prolonged period of onshore flow will lead to multiple elevated high tide cycles this week resulting in rounds of coastal flooding, with the peak being this evening.
Frost impacts possible Friday night and Saturday night where the growing season continues.

CTP.excerpt: ) Dry and seasonably mild early Autumn weather continue through this weekend and into the last week of October.

RLX.excerpt: ) High pressure ruling the roost through the weekend will continue to provide extended dry weather, with near seasonable daytime temperatures, while chilly overnights with patchy frost potential and river valley steam fog.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:26}} to {{t:49}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 39).

NWS Burlington forecasters, Wednesday 7:29 AM: "High pressure continues through Friday with increasing fire weather concerns on Thursday into Friday with slightly stronger winds and low humidity values."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.
